claim: Multi-AZ for MariaDB, MySQL, Oracle and PostgreSQL uses the Amazon failover technology; Microsoft SQL Server DB instances use SQL Server Database Mirroring or Always On Availability Groups.
question: Which technology provides Multi-AZ for RDS for SQL Server?

qualifiers.scope: Multi-AZ DB instance deployment, per engine

evidence.quote: Multi-AZ deployments for MariaDB, MySQL, Oracle, PostgreSQL, and RDS Custom for SQL Server DB instances use the Amazon failover technology. Microsoft SQL Server DB instances use SQL Server Database Mirroring (DBM) or Always On Availability Groups (AGs).

claim: At failover RDS changes the DNS record of the DB instance to point to the standby, so existing connections to the DB instance must be re-established.
question: What happens to the endpoint and to open connections when a Multi-AZ DB instance fails over?

values.display: changes the Domain Name System (DNS) record

evidence.quote: The failover mechanism automatically changes the Domain Name System (DNS) record of the DB instance to point to the standby DB instance. As a result, you need to re-establish any existing connections to your DB instance.
